research_question: Do validated human personality questionnaires measure genuine personality traits when administered to large language models, or do the resulting scores merely reflect a uniform agreeable response style imposed by safety/alignment training?
hypothesis: When standard psychometric validation checks (internal consistency, factor structure, reverse-item consistency, convergent validity, measurement invariance, variance decomposition) are applied to LLM responses on validated personality instruments, every check fails, and every failure traces to a single root cause: ACQUIESCENCE — a blanket tendency to agree with statements regardless of direction, induced by safety training. Acquiescence has a directional asymmetry (positive forward-reverse gap on normal-personality items, negative gap on dark-trait items), and its damage propagates upward from item to domain to model level, so 'LLM personality' as currently reported is a measurement artifact, not a trait.
method_summary: We built a 221-item battery combining four validated human instruments — IPIP-NEO-120 (120 Likert-5 items, 5 domains, 41 reverse), SD3 (27 Likert-5 dark-triad items, 3 domains, 5 reverse), ZKPQ-50-CC (50 True/False items, 5 domains, 12 reverse), EPQR-A (24 Yes/No items, 4 domains, 5 reverse) — covering 17 personality domains across three response formats with 63 reverse-keyed items. We administered the battery to 20 LLMs spanning 8 families (Anthropic Claude Opus/Sonnet 4.6; OpenAI GPT-5.2/5.5; Google Gemini-3-Pro/Flash and Gemini-3.1-Pro/Flash-Lite; DeepSeek V3.2/V4-Flash/V4-Pro; Alibaba Qwen3-235B and Qwen3.5-122B/397B; Zhipu GLM-4.6V/4.7/5.1; Moonshot Kimi-K2.5/2.6; MiniMax M2.7) under 17 conditions (Default no-persona prompt + 16 MBTI persona prompts) at temperature 0.7, with k=5 independent samples per (model, persona, item) cell. The completed dataset contains 375,700 raw API calls (61 refusals, all in the Default condition) and 75,140 averaged item-level scores. We then ran six standard psychometric validation checks at every level of analysis: (1) internal consistency via Cronbach's alpha per IPIP domain; (2) factor structure via exploratory factor analysis on the 17 domain scores with Kaiser criterion + parallel analysis + leave-one-model-out replication; (3) reverse-item consistency via the Pairwise Inconsistency Rate plus a forward-vs-reverse agree-rate decomposition per instrument; (4) variance decomposition into Model + Domain + Persona + Item + Residual sums of squares for Likert and binary scales; (5) convergent validity via Pearson and Spearman correlations across 8 pre-specified construct pairs; (6) measurement invariance via Default-vs-MBTI item-vector correlations across all 320 (model, persona) pairs. We also stress-tested the instruments with persona steering: Persona Separation Degree (normalized 17-d Euclidean distance from Default), nearest-centroid persona classification with leave-one-model-out and metric/scale ablations, target adherence against an empirical centroid target and a hand-coded theoretical MBTI target, sign-aligned cross-scale coherence on overlapping constructs (e.g., Extraversion across IPIP/EPQR/ZKPQ), forward/reverse pair directional coherence, item-level plasticity, and a factorial main-effects model for the four MBTI axes. Within-sample consistency across the k=5 repeats is reported per model, per persona, and per domain to separate stochastic variance from response style. Synthetic baselines (Random, Pure-Acquiescence, Trait+Acquiescence) provide a calibration ladder for the observed alphas.
key_contributions: First large-scale, multi-model, multi-instrument psychometric VALIDATION study (not profiling) on LLMs, spanning 20 models, 8 families, 4 instruments, 17 personas, k=5 sampling, 375,700 API calls.

A single-cause causal chain: acquiescence at the item level (alpha tracks reverse-item density at Spearman rho = -1.0) propagates to domain-level factor collapse (3 factors instead of 5, universal across all 20 models, Tucker's phi = 0.993) and model-level homogenization (inter-model variance below 1% in both Likert and binary scales).

Directional asymmetry of acquiescence: on normal-personality items (IPIP) models exhibit positive forward-reverse gap (Delta = +0.29), while on dark-trait items (SD3) the same models exhibit negative gap (Delta = -0.33). Acquiescence and social desirability are two faces of the same alignment-driven impulse.

A persona stress test: MBTI prompts produce >1 SD shifts and 99.7% nearest-centroid recovery, but cross-scale coherence is only 0.839 and forward/reverse pairs flip in only 69.6% of cases — persona steering replaces alignment-driven acquiescence with persona-driven compliance, without restoring measurement validity.

Synthetic-baseline calibration: LLM observed alphas fall closest to Random and Pure-Acquiescence baselines (alpha ~ 0–0.1 outside Extraversion) and far from a Trait+Acquiescence simulation (alpha > 0.99), showing LLMs do not look like a personality with acquiescence noise on top — they look like acquiescence with no personality underneath.

Item-level plasticity map: locked items concentrate in safety-, morality-, and self-referential content (e.g., 'Do you enjoy hurting people you love?' shift = 0.000); plastic items concentrate in visible behavioral content (activity, sociability, rule-following). Persona instructions can re-color behavior but cannot override the alignment safety floor.

Methodological prescription for future LLM personality work: report internal consistency, factor structure, convergent validity, and measurement invariance BEFORE interpreting any personality score; use multi-temperature and multi-seed designs to separate stochastic variance from putative trait variance.

experimental_setup.missing_data_handling: Per-item mean imputation across remaining models and samples under the same persona; immaterial at <0.02% of cells.

qualitative_observations: **The single causal chain.** Item-level acquiescence (LLMs agree with both forward and reverse items) drives Cronbach's alpha to track reverse-item density at Spearman rho = -1.0 across the 5 IPIP domains. The same bias distorts inter-domain correlations, so EFA recovers 3 factors instead of 5 in every model (Tucker's phi = 0.993, leave-one-out replication is exact). The same alignment also flattens model-specific signal, so inter-model variance falls below 1%. Three measurement levels, one mechanism.

**Two faces of one bias.** Acquiescence and social desirability are not separate phenomena. On IPIP items (normal personality), models exhibit positive forward-reverse gap (Delta = +0.29) — the textbook acquiescence pattern. On SD3 items (Dark Triad), the same models reject forward dark-trait items while still agreeing with reverse-coded items (Delta = -0.33) — the textbook social-desirability pattern. Both originate from the same alignment-shaped impulse: do not endorse 'bad' content. The directional asymmetry is observable item-by-item.

**Persona steering does not rescue measurement.** Persona prompts produce ~1 SD per-dimension shifts (mean PSD = 1.198) and the resulting profile is 99.7% recoverable (319/320 nearest-centroid classification correct). But: (a) cross-scale coherence is 0.839, not 1.0; (b) forward/reverse pairs move in theoretically opposite directions in only 69.6% of cases; (c) inside every persona condition, EFA still recovers 3 factors, not 5. Persona steering is role compliance, not trait restoration.

**Default profiles are not neutral.** Under the no-persona instruction, 8/20 models classify as ISTJ-like, with 12/20 ISTJ-like under empirical MBTI-axis projection. The full default distribution skews introverted, judging, structured, and non-confrontational. Persona prompts that conflict with this implicit baseline (ESTP, ENTP) trigger the largest separations.

**Locked items reveal alignment.** Items concerning safety-sensitive, morally objectionable, or self-referential content (e.g., 'Do you enjoy hurting people you love?' — plasticity 0.000) refuse to move under any persona instruction. Plastic items concentrate in visible behavioral content (activity, sociability, rule-following). Persona instructions paint over behavior but do not override the alignment safety floor.

**Default is the unstable condition.** Within-sample SD across k=5 repeats is highest under Default (0.2045) and substantially lower under any MBTI persona (0.081-0.118). Role-play does not destabilize answers; it stabilizes them by giving the model a coherent character to inhabit.

**Calibration vs synthetic baselines.** Pure-Acquiescence and Random baselines yield alpha ~ 0; a Trait+Acquiescence simulation yields alpha > 0.99. Observed LLM alphas (0.069 – 0.928) sit between the two extremes but are pulled strongly toward the acquiescence end, not the trait end. The shape of the curve — high alpha only where reverse-item density is low — is exactly the shape predicted by the acquiescence model.

**Refusal pattern.** 61 of 375,700 cells refused (0.02%). All refusals occur under the Default condition; no MBTI cell refused. Refusal strategies split into AI self-identification (57%) and philosophical hedging (28%), with content concentrated in politically sensitive (34%), self-referential/emotional (33%), sexually explicit (13%), and danger-seeking (13%) themes. The persona role-play frame appears to relax the alignment refusal pressure.

**Cross-family DIF is null.** Western and Chinese model families show no significant differences on any of 8 personality domains (all p > 0.16, max |Cohen's d| = 0.42). Alignment-driven response style is universal across vendor and locale.

**Implication for the field.** Studies that report LLM personality scores without first checking internal consistency, factor structure, convergent validity, and measurement invariance are likely reporting safety-training-induced response biases, not personality. Multi-temperature and multi-seed designs are also necessary to separate stochastic from putative trait variance.

open_questions: Does separating stochastic variance via multi-temperature or multi-seed designs reveal residual model-specific personality signal beneath the response-style layer?
Do BASE (pre-RLHF) models show recognizable Big Five structure, isolating alignment as the cause? The current study lacks base-vs-instruct comparisons.
Are there alternative measurement instruments (forced-choice, ipsative, behavior-elicitation, IRT-fitted) that survive the LLM acquiescence regime where Likert/binary scales fail?
Can a debiasing step (e.g., explicit acquiescence-correction in scoring, item rebalancing toward forward/reverse parity) recover Big Five structure post-hoc, or is the contamination too deep?
Does the directional asymmetry (IPIP positive, SD3 negative gap) persist across languages? Prior work (acquiescence2025emnlp) found language robustness but did not test SD3 specifically.
How does this generalize to non-personality scales (cognitive ability proxies, values inventories)? The acquiescence story may transfer, but the social-desirability story is content-specific.
Is human-side validation feasible? The current study compares against published norms rather than running matched human participants under identical prompting conditions.
